source_note: Strategic / incentive-misalignment failure modes for the L4 layer (METHODOLOGY.md §5c). Drawn from mechanism design (Akerlof, Stiglitz), agency theory (Jensen-Meckling, Hart-Holmström), rent-seeking economics (Tullock, Krueger), incomplete-contracting theory, and the political-science literature on institutional capture. Distinct from cognitive_biases.json: those entries record properties of judgment; these record properties of incentive alignment between an actor's effective objective function and their institutional mandate. Validity of any L4 entry requires all four of M1-M4 (METHODOLOGY.md §5c). Each entry carries an 'operational_signature' string — the documentary pattern the Failure-Mode Classifier looks for in the record. The 'subtype' field maps to the L4 sub-types in §5c (L4b, L4c, L4e, L4g, L4h). Sub-types L4a, L4d, L4f are reserved until v0.5; no entries here use them.

subtypes.L4b: Career / legacy protection — actor optimizes own future role, reputation, or post-tenure prospects.
subtypes.L4c: Rent-seeking — private financial or material interest of the actor or a documented closely-held network.
subtypes.L4e: Tribal / factional loyalty over mandate — outcomes correlate with documented faction line against local evidence.
subtypes.L4g: Bounded-mandate externality — actor optimizes formal mandate; foreseeable damage outside it is unaccounted.
subtypes.L4h: Persistent claim without competence-deferral — actor lacks documented capacity but persists, using procedural standing as the justifying mechanism.

modes.name: Memo-trail deferral construction
modes.definition: Actor produces a documented record whose primary function is plausible deniability for the actor in the event of a downstream bad outcome, rather than improving the decision quality.
modes.operational_signature: Memos in the actor's name show defensive structure (caveats, distributions, requests-for-confirmation) disproportionate to the analytic content; the same actor's memos on lower-stakes matters of similar complexity show no such structure.

modes.name: Decision-deferral to successor / post-tenure
modes.definition: A decision within the actor's mandate and within their tenure window is structured to fall on a successor or on a post-tenure body, where the deferral is not justified by analytic incompleteness.
modes.operational_signature: Documented deferral mechanism (commission referral, study extension, mandate transfer) lands the decision after the actor's known departure; the same record contains internal materials sufficient to decide, and no acknowledgement of the deferral's timing relative to the tenure window.

modes.name: Insulation-by-delegation
modes.definition: Decision is delegated to a body or office from which the consequence cannot meaningfully return to the originating actor for accountability — not by mandate-fit but by accountability-distance.
modes.operational_signature: Delegation route bypasses bodies with closer subject-matter expertise in favor of bodies with weaker accountability links to the originating actor; rationale for the route is procedural rather than substantive.

modes.name: Revolving-door alignment
modes.definition: Actor's decision favors an entity with which the actor has a documented prior or prospective employment, advisory, or board relationship.
modes.operational_signature: The receiving entity appears in the actor's prior employment history, post-government employment within a short window, or in documented negotiations during the decision period; the decision is favorable to that entity beyond what the public record's merit analysis supports.

modes.name: Equity-position alignment
modes.definition: Actor or documented close family / trust holds a financial position whose value is materially affected by the decision, and the position is not blind-trusted, divested, or recused.
modes.operational_signature: Disclosure filings, court records, or credible reporting establish the holding; the holding is in the regulated counter-party or its documented dependents; no recusal or divestment is on the record.

modes.name: Network-concentrated allocation
modes.definition: Contracts, appointments, exemptions, or authorizations concentrate in a documented family / professional / political / religious network at a rate beyond what the qualified-pool composition predicts.
modes.operational_signature: Allocation distribution shows statistical concentration in a definable network; the network membership predates the allocation; the qualification justification, if offered, does not address the concentration.

modes.name: Faction-line voting against local evidence
modes.definition: On a technical or evidentiary matter, the actor's vote or stated position aligns with the faction line in cases where the locally available evidence supports the opposite outcome.
modes.operational_signature: Multiple peer voters with comparable access to the same record split along faction lines on a matter where the evidence is technically (not ideologically) determinable; the actor's stated reasoning does not address the technical record but invokes principle, identity, or solidarity terms.

modes.name: Faction-aligned appointments overriding qualification
modes.definition: Appointments to technical / regulatory / oversight roles preferentially select faction-aligned candidates over candidates whose documented qualifications more closely match the role's published criteria.
modes.operational_signature: Appointee's qualifications fall short of the published criteria on at least one named axis; faction-aligned appointee pattern across multiple appointments under the same actor is documentable; rejected stronger candidates are documentable through public application records or reporting.

modes.name: Externality omitted from rationale
modes.definition: Decision rationale optimizes the actor's formal mandate; foreseeable damage outside the mandate is documented in pre-decision analyses available to the actor but is absent from the decision rationale.
modes.operational_signature: Pre-decision analyses (working-level memos, commissioned studies, peer-agency briefings) establish the externality; the decision's published rationale does not engage with it; the omission is not justified by an information-availability argument that survives §5b A1-A3.

modes.name: Externality dismissed without engagement
modes.definition: The externality is acknowledged in the decision rationale but is dismissed by category ("out of scope", "another body's responsibility") without analytic engagement with its magnitude or distribution.
modes.operational_signature: Decision text contains a reference to the externality and a category-level dismissal; no quantitative or institutional-incidence analysis is attached; no cross-body coordination is documented as an alternative handling.

modes.name: Mandate-boundary exploitation
modes.definition: Actor structures the decision so that its costs fall predominantly outside the actor's mandate scope while its benefits fall inside — even where alternative structures with more even cost/benefit distribution were available.
modes.operational_signature: Comparison of the chosen design with documented alternatives shows the chosen design concentrates externalized cost; the alternatives were on the record at decision time; no published rationale addresses the cost-distribution asymmetry.

modes.name: Procedural-equality assertion against expertise
modes.definition: Actor without the documented technical, factual, or jurisdictional capacity for the call invokes procedural standing (right to be heard, equality of voice, due-process objection) as the basis for blocking, delaying, or overriding the substantive determination, when a deferral channel was available and was not used.
modes.operational_signature: Actor's qualification gap is documentable on the record; the actor's intervention is procedural rather than substantive; an available deferral mechanism (referral, recusal, expert opinion) is documented as having been declined or not invoked; the substantive determination is delayed, modified, or reversed as a result.

modes.name: Delay-as-veto without substantive opposition
modes.definition: Actor uses procedural delay tools (continuances, additional-review requests, point-of-order objections) repeatedly on a matter where the actor neither argues nor commissions substantive opposition; the cumulative delay achieves the effect of opposition without the burden of making a case.
modes.operational_signature: Delay actions cluster on one matter; actor's record on that matter contains no substantive analytic position; the delay timing aligns with windows where ratification, deadline-expiry, or external event would render the matter moot.

modes.name: Deferral-channel non-use under capacity gap
modes.definition: Actor proceeds with a determination on a matter outside their documented capacity even though a deferral channel (technical advisory body, recusal mechanism, formal expert opinion request) was available and within their power to invoke.
modes.operational_signature: Capacity gap is documentable; deferral channel exists in the body's published procedures; actor did not invoke the channel; no documented justification for non-use that addresses the capacity gap.
